# Warp

> Warp is an MIT-licensed .NET 10 library for background jobs, pub/sub messages, in-process requests and streams. It stores work in your own PostgreSQL or SQL Server database through your EF Core DbContext (transactional outbox, no message broker) and ships a real-time operations dashboard.

Facts an agent should get right:

- NuGet package ids are `Moberg.Warp.*`; namespaces are `Warp.*`. Use the same version for every package.
- Packages: `Moberg.Warp.Core` (always), `Moberg.Warp.Worker` (the server), one provider (`Moberg.Warp.Provider.PostgreSql` or `Moberg.Warp.Provider.SqlServer`), `Moberg.Warp.Dashboard`. Optional: `Moberg.Warp.Http`, `Moberg.Warp.Adapters.Http`, `Moberg.Warp.Adapters.Refit`.
- Register with `AddWarpServer<TContext>(opt => { opt.UsePostgreSql(); })` in a process that runs jobs, `AddWarp<TContext>` in one that only publishes. `AddWarpWorker` no longer exists.
- Contracts and handlers: `IJob` / `IJobHandler<T>`, `IMessage` / `IMessageHandler<T>`, `IRequest<TResponse>` / `IRequestHandler<T, TResponse>`, `IStreamRequest<TResponse>` / `IStreamRequestHandler<T, TResponse>`. A source generator registers handlers; there is nothing to register by hand.
- Publish with `IPublisher` (`Enqueue`, `Schedule`, `Publish`), then call `SaveChangesAsync` on the same DbContext: the job commits with your data.
- Requires .NET 10 and PostgreSQL 17/18 or SQL Server 2022/2025.
- Source: https://github.com/moberghr/warp. Every page below is plain Markdown; any docs URL also works with `.md` appended.

## Start here

- [Why Warp](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/why-warp.md): What Warp is, what it replaces (Hangfire, MediatR, a broker-backed outbox), and when another tool fits better
- [Getting Started](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/getting-started.md): Packages, DbContext setup, AddWarpServer / AddWarp registration, migrations, first handler
- [Patterns Overview](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/patterns.md): The four patterns, the type hierarchy, and the IPipelineBehavior pipeline they share
- [Jobs](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/patterns/jobs.md): IJob with one handler: enqueue, schedule, retries, continuations, batches, named queues
- [Messages](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/patterns/messages.md): Pub/sub IMessage: every handler runs as its own job, fan-out routing
- [Requests and Streams](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/patterns/requests.md): In-process IRequest<TResponse> via IMediator.Send() and IStreamRequest<TResponse> via CreateStream(), no persistence

## Jobs and workflows

- [Outbox Pattern](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/outbox-pattern.md): Transactional outbox: a job is saved in the same transaction as your business data
- [Recurring Jobs](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/recurring-jobs.md): Cron-based scheduling, deduplication, execution history
- [Sagas](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/sagas.md): Correlated stateful workflows, [Correlate] / [StartsSaga], delete-on-completion
- [Background Services](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/background-services.md): WarpBackgroundService supervisor loops, PerServer / Singleton lease scope
- [Job Metadata](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/metadata.md): Key-value metadata, publish pipeline behaviors, IJobContext
- [Job Cancellation](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/cancellation.md): Graceful CancellationMode, handler CancellationToken, transitive batch cancel
- [Pause / Resume](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/pause.md): Pause servers and worker groups, resume processing
- [DB-Generated IDs](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/db-generated-ids.md): Database-assigned identifiers

## Flow control

- [Mutex](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/mutex.md): [Mutex] key-based mutual exclusion for jobs
- [Semaphore](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/semaphore.md): Bounded concurrency (limit > 1) via [Semaphore], Wait / Skip policies
- [Rate Limiting](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/rate-limit.md): Fixed / sliding / token-bucket styles, Skip vs Wait, per-key buckets
- [Timeout](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/timeout.md): Per-attempt / total deadlines, Delete vs Fail modes
- [Circuit Breaker](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/circuit-breaker.md): Trip on failure threshold, half-open probe recovery
- [No-Restart](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/no-restart.md): [NoRestart] / [Restart] for non-idempotent work and stale-job recovery

## Performance

- [Performance](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/performance.md): Per-job cost, how Warp keeps database load low, settings for throughput
- [Warp vs Hangfire](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/performance/warp-vs-hangfire.md): Measured throughput, statements, CPU, WAL and allocation per job on PostgreSQL
- [Batched Completions](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/batched-completions.md): Dispatcher mode and coalesced completion writes
- [Database Push](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/db-push.md): LISTEN/NOTIFY and Service Broker wake-up, opt-in low-latency pickup
- [Memory Benchmarks](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/operations/benchmarks.md): Memory benchmarks that verify the server does not leak

## HTTP and integrations

- [HTTP Endpoints](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/http.md): Expose IRequest<T> / IStreamRequest<T> handlers as ASP.NET endpoints via [WarpHttp...] attributes (inbound)
- [Outbound Adapters](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/adapters.md): Observe outbound calls to other services, cluster-shared rate limiting, capture on failure (AddAdapters)
- [Durable Webhooks](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/webhooks.md): Durable outbound webhook delivery: retries, signing, redelivery, exhaustion (built into Core, always on)

## Observability

- [Job Tracing](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/tracing.md): TraceId and SpawnedByJobId: one trace across every job and message a request started
- [Multi-Application Observability](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/applications.md): Many applications on one schema, each identified and filterable in the dashboard
- [Queue Metrics](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/queue-metrics.md): Queue wait and backlog depth per queue
- [Error Grouping](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/error-grouping.md): Failures from jobs, endpoints, adapters and the browser grouped into issues by fingerprint
- [SLOs and Error Budgets](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/slo-error-budget.md): Objectives over Warp's own aggregates, error budget and burn rate
- [Custom Metrics](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/custom-metrics.md): Collect your own System.Diagnostics.Metrics instruments, chart them, hold them to an SLO
- [Metrics Retention Tiers](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/metrics-retention.md): How counters roll up into hourly and daily tiers and how long each is kept
- [Endpoint Observability](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/endpoint-observability.md): Observe inbound requests to Warp HTTP endpoints: caller, duration, status, bodies
- [Client Observability](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/client-observability.md): Browser errors, Core Web Vitals, logs and custom events through the ingest endpoint
- [Observability Sinks and OpenTelemetry](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/observability-sinks.md): Meters, activity sources and sinks for exporting what Warp records
- [Operational Notifications](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/operational-notifications.md): IWarpNotifier: hand operational events (webhook exhausted, instance down) to your own channel
- [Dashboard Push](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/features/dashboard-push.md): SignalR realtime dashboard updates

## Operations

- [Configuration](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/operations/configuration.md): Workers, polling, retention, dispatcher mode, worker groups, schema, naming conventions
- [EF Core Integration](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/operations/ef-core-integration.md): DbContext setup, the server-internal context, migrations, naming conventions
- [Connection Pooling](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/operations/connection-pooling.md): Which lock shapes need a session-mode connection; transaction-mode poolers (Neon -pooler, Supabase 6543, Azure 6432)
- [Crash Recovery](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/operations/crash-recovery.md): Sliding invisibility timeout, keep-alive, stale job recovery
- [Dashboard Auth](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/operations/dashboard-auth.md): MapWarpDashboard + RequireAuthorization, built-in cookie login, localhost-only
- [Multi-Project Source Generation](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/operations/multi-project-source-gen.md): How the source generators find handlers across several projects

## Upgrading and migrating

- [Upgrading to 8.0](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/operations/upgrading-to-8.md): What to change going from 7.7 to 8.0: handler saves, index migration, rolling deploy
- [Migrating from Hangfire](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/operations/migrating-from-hangfire.md): API mapping, what changes in how a job is written, gradual migration
- [Migrating from Wolverine](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/operations/migrating-from-wolverine.md): API mapping and wiring differences
- [Releases](https://moberghr.github.io/warp/docs/releases.md): Version history and upgrade notes
